notes.text: Questions are title-domain screens with 5 buttons over a held picture (A/B/C answers, D = PASS, centre = BANK); the answer labels and question text are in the video. Every answer button runs the same 'g[13]=0, LinkTailPGC'; the POST reads HL_BTNN (SPRM8) and branches, so the key is only visible by pressing each answer in the VM (tools/quiz_key.py --vm).
notes.why: Comparing button commands picks PASS as the 'odd one out'; that was wrong.

notes.text: g[8] is a clock (counter mode): 'if (g[8] <= 0x3e8) LinkPGCN 2' is time running out. Offline it never counts, so key derivation sets it first: --setup x7100000875300000 (g[8] = 30000).
notes.why: Without it every answer reads as a timeout and all paths are the same.

notes.text: On the rig the verdict is g[7], the money chain: a right answer raises it by 2 (0, 2, 4, ...), a wrong one resets it to 0; a right answer also adds 2 to g[14] and plays feedback cell 3 then PGC 4 -> 5, a wrong one cells 5/7 then straight to PGC 5. The offline paths (VTS 2 PGC 1378 cell 3 vs cell 2) are a cold-start artefact: the rig, mid-game, never visits them.
notes.why: answers_right compares PGC paths -> 18/18 'no data' (2026-10-23, wl_answer2); the wrong-answer control arm (wl_wrong1) showed g[7] separates the two both ways.

notes.text: Question banks: VTS 3-19 and 24-28 hold 50 questions each, VTS 20 and 29 hold 13 (1,126 keyed screens). VTS 21-23 are menus: TT/21/30/1 is SELECT THE NUMBER OF PLAYERS, not a question.
notes.why: quiz_key keyed the player-count menu until the split-step rule required the wrong answers to agree on a real step.

explore.description: Start the disc and let the autoplayer play what it recognises for 5 minutes; then: tools/hil_disc.py explored <run dir>

answer.description: Walk the menus with default Selects and, at every question the VM keys cover, give the right answer for 5 minutes: every answer must take the right-answer path.

answer_wrong.description: The control arm of 'answer': the same run aiming at a WRONG answer on every keyed question (quiz_key pick='wrong'). The right/wrong evidence must read wrong here, or answers_right cannot tell the two apart.

quiz.note: g[8] (the clock) = 30000 so offline answers are not timeouts
